payload.title: What Are the Serbian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
protect_keywords: quirky serbian wedding traditions (old URL; SEO to quantify US and AU)
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a generous budget, often with a Serbian-Australian partner or parent, who want to understand each Serbian custom in the order it happens, which belong to the Serbian Orthodox service and which are family folk custom, and whether to hold the wedding in Serbia (Smartraveller: exercise normal safety precautions) or carry the customs into a wedding in Australia or another destination.
payload.goal: Read the free Wedded Wonderland digital magazine (primary CTA); secondary, in-context invitation to speak with a Wedded Advisor placed after the 'bringing the customs to your wedding' section.
payload.angle: A Serbian wedding is a sequence held together by two people, the kum and kuma: the prosidba, the barjak leading the svatovi to collect and 'buy' the bride, the apple, then the Orthodox rite of rings, crowning, common cup and the walk around the table, the welcome at the groom's home and the kolo. We walk 10 to 11 customs in that order, source the church parts from the Serbian Orthodox Church (including its Australian diocese) and the folk parts from museum, ministry and UNESCO pages, label the rest 'often told', correct the myths that circulate (mirrors and garlic, the kum as a simple 'best man'), and, because Smartraveller rates Serbia 'exercise normal safety precautions', show Serbian-Australian couples both paths: marrying in Serbia with the embassy and registry steps checked, or bringing the customs home through their parish.
must_include: One early framing line: the church rite is set by the Serbian Orthodox Church; the folk customs around it vary by family and region
Customs in order, grouped 'Before and at the church' (1 to 7) and 'The celebration' (8 to 10 or 11), each numbered
The kum and kuma as the thread through the day, only where sourced
Orthodox service from official church sources (rings, crowning, common cup, walking around the table); 'ask your parish priest' for requirements
Kolo with UNESCO 'Kolo, traditional folk dance' (Serbia, 2017) only as far as its text goes

Section for Australians: Smartraveller level and date (as at November 2026), Australian Embassy in Belgrade (CNI, notarial), 'Getting married overseas' for recognition, registry 'check with the registry and the embassy, including any fees'; diaspora weddings in Australia via parish
FAQ of 5 to 7 questions with no amounts

tradition_plan.note: Planner (wedding-planner-sme) runs batch A and batch B in parallel, scratch folders 02-research/batch-a and 02-research/batch-b, 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, no extra sourcing rounds. Preferred sources: Serbian Orthodox Church official pages (spc.rs; Diocese of Australia and New Zealand), ich.unesco.org, Ethnographic Museum in Belgrade, Serbia's Ministry of Culture, serbia.travel, Britannica, academic journals, Australian Embassy Belgrade, Smartraveller. Never competitor wedding sites, vendor blogs, scribd, serbia.com, Wikipedia, lifestyle magazines. Unsourced: 'often told', no meanings as fact, no [[VERIFY]] marker. Serbian terms with diacritics as the source gives them (Latin script). One honest framing line per section. Culture, not politics; no virginity or 'proof' customs.
tradition_plan.count: 10 customs plus optional item 11 plus the legal section (batch A: 7 customs; batch B: 3 customs, optional 11, legal)
